item.text: Agence Europe reports that the Irish Presidency asked ambassadors on 11 November to clarify the partner origin concept, reciprocity and the low-carbon method. No clear majority backs its latest low-carbon compromise.
Agence Europe reports that France, now backed by Germany, wants the Made in Europe scope extended to Switzerland and the United Kingdom. The automotive provisions went to Coreper on 11 November.
Euractiv reports that the Irish Presidency dropped language on cross-border clinical trials from its Biotech Act draft. EU countries are split over how to help patients join trials abroad.
Euractiv reports that Laura Ballarín Cereza (S&D), rapporteur on the KIDS Act, expects backing for a ban for under-15s. She also wants age limits for risky AI systems.

Agence Europe reports that António Costa's negotiating box of 21 November sets the MFF 2028–2034 at €1,582bn in 2025 prices, €180.5bn (10%) below the Commission proposal, and adds a 3% digital services tax.

Agence Europe reports that co-rapporteur Siegfried Mureşan called Costa's proposal unacceptable. Germany, the Netherlands and Sweden said it is still too large, and France called it very disappointing.

MLex reports that Parliament's committee vote on the Industrial Accelerator Act is set for 1 December, with compromises on the main political questions not yet agreed. Anna Cavazzini said the EPP is engaging constructively.

EUobserver reports that the Irish Presidency is on its third Industrial Accelerator Act compromise without a deal. A minority led by France wants the list of countries that count as Made in Europe kept short.
MLex reports that IMCO's opinion on the Digital Omnibus recommends exempting cloud providers from some switching obligations for certain older contracts.
